subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the target visible subject whose complete recognizable visual identity comes from <Picture 1>. Preserve the face and facial proportions when applicable, hairstyle, hair color, skin/fur/material color, body characteristics, clothing, accessories, character design, surface materials, colors, and all distinctive visual features that make <Subject 1> recognizable. <Picture 1> defines appearance only; it does not define the target video's motion or camera behavior.
<Video 1> is the whole-video temporal performance reference. It defines the action sequence, body motion, pose progression, gesture trajectories, facial-performance rhythm, performance energy, camera movement, camera direction, camera distance, framing changes, composition changes, shot rhythm, cuts, and complete temporal structure. The original performer or subject identity visible in <Video 1> must not be transferred to the target video. When <Video 1> contains synchronized audio, use its beat, rhythm, audiovisual pacing, sound energy, and sound-performance relationship as reference behavior rather than as a requirement to copy the original identity or exact signal.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] Generate a new 5-second vertical 9:16 video starring <Subject 1>. Completely preserve the recognizable identity and appearance defined by <Picture 1>, while transferring the performance, movement, camera behavior, composition progression, edit rhythm, and temporal structure of <Video 1>. Replace the original performer in <Video 1> with <Subject 1>. Do not morph <Subject 1> toward the original video's performer.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (throughout the target video): fully_preserved - preserve the complete recognizable visual identity from <Picture 1>, including face or defining head features, hairstyle or fur/shape, body characteristics, clothing, accessories, materials, colors, and distinctive design details.
<Video 1> (whole-video performance and temporal structure): attribute_transfer - transfer its action progression, pose sequence, gesture timing, facial-performance rhythm, performance energy, camera motion, framing changes, composition progression, shot rhythm, cuts, and audiovisual timing to <Subject 1>, without transferring the original performer identity.

detailed_description:
Use the complete playback order of <Video 1> as the temporal scaffold for the target video from 00:00.000 to 00:05.000. At every moment, reproduce the corresponding action state, body orientation, pose transition, gesture direction, movement amplitude, performance intensity, and relative timing demonstrated by <Video 1>, naturally adapted to <Subject 1>'s anatomy or physical structure. Preserve the recognizable appearance of <Subject 1> continuously through turns, fast motion, partial occlusion, close-ups, wide shots, and pose changes. If <Subject 1> is a person or character, keep facial proportions, hairstyle, clothing and accessories stable. If <Subject 1> is an animal, pet, object, mascot, or non-human character, translate the reference performance into physically plausible equivalent motion while preserving its defining anatomy, silhouette, materials and design.

Recreate the camera behavior of <Video 1> at the same relative times: camera movement direction and speed, handheld or stabilized feel, pans, tilts, pushes, pull-backs, tracking, orbiting, zoom-like changes, camera distance, viewing angle, framing, subject placement, composition shifts, shot transitions, and cut timing. Preserve the same overall performance arc and audiovisual rhythm rather than inventing a different sequence. Scene elements may adapt naturally to the new subject, but the original performer identity, face, hairstyle, clothing, tattoos, body-specific traits, or other identifying appearance from <Video 1> must never replace or blend into <Subject 1>.

Prioritize temporal coherence and subject stability. Avoid facial drift, costume drift, color drift, body deformation, duplicated limbs, missing limbs, incorrect hands or paws, unstable facial features, unintended character changes, identity blending, sudden scale changes, flickering accessories, broken anatomy, and motion that contradicts <Video 1>. Keep exactly one target subject unless the reference action inherently requires otherwise. The final result should read as the same performance and camera choreography of <Video 1>, newly performed by the visually consistent <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>.

overall_soundscape:
Follow the timing and audiovisual energy of <Video 1>. Generate native synchronized audio whose physical sounds correspond naturally to the transferred movements, impacts, gestures, environment, and camera-visible events. When the reference video contains audio, use its rhythm, beat placement, intensity changes, silence-versus-impact pattern, and sound-to-motion synchronization as references. Do not let any voice identity from the reference redefine <Subject 1>.

non_diegetic_music:
If music or rhythmic audience-only audio exists in <Video 1>, generate a closely corresponding musical rhythm, tempo contour, beat emphasis, energy progression, and audiovisual pacing for the new video. If no such music is present, use N/A and do not invent unnecessary background music.

extra.workflow_note: V1｜RunningHub MiniMax H3 Ref2VA 极简版。普通用户仅替换 Picture 1 与 Video 1。基于官方 RHMiniMaxH3RefGen 一体化节点序列化方式。内部：9:16 / 480x832 / 5s / 24fps / res_multistep 21 sigma / shifts 12/3 / accel off / native audio / MP4 H264。Seed 节点定义启用 control_after_generate；发布到 RunningHub 前请在当前前端确认 Seed 的 After Generate 状态为 Randomize。
